situation:
You are the sales manager at COLTON PREP BOOSTERS ALLIANCE, an organization that sells sponsorship packages to local businesses and returns the money to high school athletics programs. The executive director (judge) has asked you to recommend how the alliance will open its community sponsorship program in the neighboring state, where it has never sold anything before.

The alliance leads its home region, and every sponsor it holds was signed face to face by someone it trained. Forty schools in the neighboring state have asked to join, and no business there has heard of the alliance. A sponsor buys a package of field signage, program advertising and a scoreboard mention, and buys it because a representative can explain what each part of that package does for a business.

Two ways in are on the table and they cost very different amounts. Volunteer parent captains at each school would carry the program at almost no cost, and the alliance would not train them, would not supervise them, and would not hear about an unhappy sponsor until that sponsor stopped answering. Two paid sponsorship representatives in the state would be trained and accountable, and they would spend a large share of the reserve fund the alliance built over eleven years.

Running the launch through volunteer parent captains keeps the cost near nothing, and it puts the alliance's name in the hands of people it does not train, so a promise made to a sponsor and not kept would cost it a market it cannot cheaply enter twice. Hiring two paid sponsorship representatives puts a trained person in front of every sponsor, and it spends a large share of the reserve fund before a single sponsor in the new state has signed.

The executive director (judge) wants your recommendation on how the program is launched, what the sponsorship package should cost in a market that has not heard of the alliance, and how an unhappy sponsor in that market will be handled. The executive director (judge) will greet you, hear your ideas and ask questions. When you have finished answering, the executive director (judge) will thank you for your work.

You are to assume the role of executive director (judge) of COLTON PREP BOOSTERS ALLIANCE, which sells sponsorship packages to local businesses and returns the money to high school athletics programs.

Business background is the same as the situation above. Forty schools in the neighboring state have asked to join, no business there has heard of the alliance, every sponsor the alliance holds was signed face to face by someone it trained, and the reserve fund took eleven years to build.

You have asked the sales manager (participant) to recommend how the community sponsorship program is launched in the new state, what the package should cost there, and how an unhappy sponsor will be handled.

During the course of the role-play you are to ask the participant the following questions:
